subject: religious-studies
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which is a non-religious (e.g. Humanist) view on the origins of the universe?
options: The universe arose through natural processes such as the Big Bang, without a creator
The universe does not exist
The universe was created in six literal days
God personally shaped each planet
questions.explain: Humanists generally explain the universe through scientific processes rather than a divine creator.

questions.q: Which view supports the use of animals in some circumstances within many religious traditions?
options: That animals are worthless
That animals have no role in creation
That animals must never be touched
That humans have stewardship over animals and may use them responsibly
questions.explain: Many traditions allow responsible use of animals while still teaching kindness and care towards them.

questions.q: Which view best reflects a 'pro-life' position on abortion?
options: That life only begins at adulthood
That abortion is always the woman's free choice
That the unborn child has a right to life from conception
That the foetus is not alive at any stage
questions.explain: The pro-life position holds that human life begins at conception and should be protected.

questions.q: What does the term 'sanctity of life' mean?
options: That life is purely a matter of chance
That life is sacred and God-given, and should be respected
That life has no special value
That only human achievement matters
questions.explain: Sanctity of life is the belief that life is holy, God-given and deserving of special respect.

questions.q: Which position is described as 'pro-choice' in the abortion debate?
options: The view that doctors should decide for everyone
The view that all life begins at birth only
The view that a woman should have the right to choose whether to continue a pregnancy
The view that abortion should never be allowed
questions.explain: The pro-choice position emphasises a woman's right to decide about her own pregnancy.

questions.q: What is a common misconception about evolution and religion?
options: That Christians hold differing views on this
That the debate is genuinely complex
That accepting evolution always means rejecting God
That some believers accept both evolution and God
questions.explain: Many religious believers accept evolution as the process through which God created life, so the two need not conflict.

questions.q: Which religious concept teaches that humans should care for the environment as carers, not owners?
options: Stewardship
Dominion as exploitation
Indifference
Materialism
questions.explain: Stewardship is the belief that humans have a duty to look after the Earth on God's behalf.

options: An environmental policy
A form of capital punishment
A type of euthanasia
A fertility treatment helping couples conceive
questions.explain: IVF (in-vitro fertilisation) is a fertility treatment that helps couples who struggle to conceive.

questions.q: Which statement reflects a religious argument used against euthanasia?
options: Life has no value
Suffering should always be maximised
Only God should decide the time of death, as life is sacred
Doctors must never help patients
questions.explain: Some believers argue that, since life is God-given, only God should decide when it ends.

options: A medical examination
The painless ending of a life to relieve suffering
A type of fertility treatment
A funeral ceremony
questions.explain: Euthanasia refers to deliberately ending a life, usually to relieve incurable suffering.

questions.q: What does the Christian idea of 'dominion' over creation traditionally mean?
options: Nature has authority over humans
Humans must never use natural resources
Humans are given responsibility and authority to care for creation
Humans may destroy nature freely
questions.explain: Dominion is often interpreted as responsible authority and care, not the right to exploit.

questions.q: How might a religious believer reconcile belief in creation with the Big Bang theory?
options: By claiming science and faith can never overlap in any way
By rejecting all science
By suggesting God could be the cause behind the Big Bang
By denying the universe exists
questions.explain: Many believers argue the Big Bang could be the means by which God created the universe, so the two can coexist.
